items.english: "But Father will worry when he comes back, so I cannot go too far," said Mitsuyo, restless on her feet. "Why, from your room the whole of this ground is in sight. And you have me to attend you, though I grant I am a rather doubtful escort, but I mean to give you nothing to trouble yourself about. If you dislike it, however, there is no help for it."
notes: Mitsuyo's first line uses chichi for her father; Tatsuya answers in his usual light coaxing without pause for speaker tags in the Japanese.

items.english: She could hardly say outright that she disliked it, and hung back. Tatsuya saw her unwillingness and went on lightly, "If I go plodding about alone I am soon weary and dull, and just as I was wishing for company you came here, that is your fate. It may trouble you, but do keep me company a little. In return I will grant you whatever unreasonable thing you ask," he said familiarly.

Unable to refuse, Mitsuyo yielded at last. It was morning. The sky was clear as if its depth had been turned outward, the white clouds of the peaks with nowhere to go, the snow lingering on the high ridges all the more vivid, piled indigo before and congealed ink behind, and as they went among swaying pampas grass and wild chrysanthemums and valerian, the stones grew ever thicker and the pines ever finer, and the glittering face of the lake met their eyes at once.
notes: Kept the kanbun-coloured landscape phrases piled indigo and congealed ink as written rather than smoothing them into plain colour words.

items.english: Bent on winning her goodwill at every step, Tatsuya chose of set purpose to take the innocent part. From idle gossip of the world he passed to amusing things in fashion, leapt to the theatre and went to music, and spared no pains of every kind. Mitsuyo gave only answering replies, and never opened her mouth of herself.

data.say: Drafted the walk invitation and lakeside passage with coaxing dialogue and unpruned scenery.
